title: "Course Schedule"
subtitle: "Ten chapters, ten mysteries, one toolkit"
---

## How the course is structured

Ten sessions in three parts. Each session has the same shape: a real puzzle drawn from public MNH data, a named protagonist whose story carries the chapter, three or four big ideas built up through the story, a "Try it yourself" springboard scenario, and a single key takeaway.

Read the slide deck before class. Run the R code on the companion page after class. Bring questions to the next session.

## Part 1 — Draw the Picture

| Session | Chapter | Country | The mystery |
|---------|---------|---------|-------------|
| **1** | [Ch 1 — Did It Actually Work?](chapters/ch01.qmd) | Ethiopia | Maternal mortality fell. 38,000 Health Extension Workers were trained. But most births were still happening at home. So what was actually working? |
| **2** | [Ch 2 — Drawing the Picture](chapters/ch02.qmd) | Rwanda | Newborn mortality halved in twenty years, with volunteers doing most of the front-line work. How can volunteers with six days of training drive that much change? |
| **3** | [Ch 3 — Building the Picture from Scratch](chapters/ch03.qmd) | Kenya | An M&E officer with one week, a budget for petrol, and one question — *why is our county not improving as fast as the neighbouring county?* |

## Part 2 — Add the Numbers

| Session | Chapter | Country | The mystery |
|---------|---------|---------|-------------|
| **4** | [Ch 4 — Putting Numbers on the Picture](chapters/ch04.qmd) | Tanzania | Tanzania's national maternal mortality ratio is 524 per 100,000 — but a midwife in Mwanza delivers 100 mothers a year. How do you make a national number useful at the bedside? |
| **5** | [Ch 5 — When New Evidence Arrives](chapters/ch05.qmd) | Ethiopia | A regional director sees deaths jump 56% in one quarter. Three explanations sit on the table. New evidence arrives in pieces over the next two weeks. How should her belief move? |
| **6** | [Ch 6 — When the Data Lies in Two Directions](chapters/ch06.qmd) | Kenya / Tanzania | A voucher programme looks like a 26-point success in the aggregate. Split by income, the relationship reverses. Same data. Opposite story. Which to trust? |

## Part 3 — Make Decisions

| Session | Chapter | Country | The mystery |
|---------|---------|---------|-------------|
| **7** | [Ch 7 — From Understanding to Deciding](chapters/ch07.qmd) | Kenya | One envelope, one new midwife, two facilities competing. Where does she go — and how do you defend the call at a public budget hearing? |
| **8** | [Ch 8 — Spreading the Money](chapters/ch08.qmd) | All four countries | A programme officer with a fixed budget across four countries. Concentrate? Spread? Tier? Each strategy has a different shape of risk. |
| **9** | [Ch 9 — When the Other Side Reacts](chapters/ch09.qmd) | Kenya | Two county directors get the same matching grant. One accepts enthusiastically. The other quietly redirects to roads. Same deal. Opposite responses. Why? |
| **10** | [Ch 10 — Can the Computer Just Tell Us?](chapters/ch10.qmd) | Tanzania | A data scientist with ten years of DHIS2 data and a director who says *"just run an algorithm"*. Can a computer actually discover causal arrows? Partly. The "no" matters more than the "yes". |

## What each session looks like

1. **The mystery (slide 2)** — a real MNH puzzle, with a public-source citation
2. **The protagonist (slide 3)** — a named mother, nurse, or analyst (composite, clearly labeled)
3. **The chapter's three or four ideas** — each grounded in the protagonist's specific situation
4. **The resolution** — the mystery from slide 2 reframed by the new ideas
5. **Try it yourself** — a springboard scenario the learner takes home
6. **The R workshop** *(on the companion page, not on the slides)*
7. **The one thing to remember** — a single sentence the chapter is built around
